newsitem.title: USA: HBO to launch new service on USSB.
newsitem.headline: HBO to launch new service on USSB.

text.p: Home Box Office, the cable television network, will add a new family-oriented service for distribution on U.S. Satellite Broadcasting Co's direct TV operation, officials from the two companies said on Thursday.

The new movie-based service, HBO Family, will be formally announced on Friday, and launched on June 1 on USSB. The 24-hour channel will be operated commercial-free, with Hollywood movies comprising 80 percent of the programming, and the remaining 20 percent original programming, including documentaries, animated features, and HBO specials.

The programming will be divided into three segments: a "Kid's Block," from 6 a.m. to 1 p.m., with movies like "Harriet the Spy," and original programming such as "Babar." The block will be repeated from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m.
A feature film will run from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m., rated G or PG. From 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., the network will feature films rated G, PG, and PG-13, but intended "for a more mature audience."
The programming service has been running on a limited basis on a few cable TV systems, officials said.
USSB's service currently reaches about five million subscribers in the United States.
HBO is a unit of Time Warner Inc.
